newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Allied Domecq profits set to slip.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Allied Domecq profits set to slip.

text.p: Drinks to ice cream group Allied Domecq Plc is expected to report lower first half profits on Wednesday, as weak sales and poor margins continue to drain profits from its spirits division.
Analysts forecasts are centred on pretax profits of 315 million stg, ranging from 304 to 325 million stg, down from 321 million stg last time. A dividend of 9.63p is forecast, up from 9.44p.

On average, analysts calculate the spirits and wine division will show a five percent fall in trading profit to 245 million, as sales remain flat and price rises overall are confined to 1.0-1.5 percent.
The group's retail division though, which includes brands Big Steak Pubs as well as Dunkin' Donuts should show an 11 percent increase in trading profit to about 120 million stg.

The company is also expected to benefit from a lower interest charge, a saving of about 25 million on last year to give 55 million, after the disposal of Ardbeg distillery and Exchange diner bars helped reduce debt.
"I'm not looking for miracles, just signs that their markets are improving," said Goldman Sachs analyst Colin Davies, who is expecting pretax profits of 309 million.
"Sentiment towards the company remains adverse but on the numbers, I think the shares are a bit oversold," he added.

Allied shares stood 7-1/2p lower at 428p at midday on Friday. They have underperformed the market by 55 percent and the management faces growing criticism from shareholders looking for a return on their investment.

There remain lingering doubts in the market also about Allied's interest in Carlsberg-Tetley. Bass hopes to acquire the brewer, but many analysts expect the new incoming Labour government to take a tougher line on the merger.

If the deal is blocked by government, then Bass has the option sell on to Carlsberg for 110 million stg, all of the stake acquired from Allied, which would in turn reimburse Bass 30 million. Allied would also have to pay Carlsberg 33 million stg for a 15 percent stake in the re-formed Carlsberg-Tetley.
"Until we hear more abnout the Carlsberg-Tetley deal we will keep them as a sell," said SocGen analyst Nick Lyall.
There are also concerns about Allied's ability to grow future profits.

"The reason for this lack of growth is easy -- a lack of cash, so that Allied cannot easily fund the needed massive increase in ad spending nor the massive increase in capex needed for UK retail," said Lehman Bros analyst John Wakely.
In February, chairman Sir Christopher Hogg said the group's trading and financial performance in the five months to January 31, 1997 had been broadly in line with expectations.
"We are therefore on course to meet our growth objectives for the year but the growth will be concentrated in the second half," he said in a statement.
He warned if sterling stays at its current levels for the rest of the year it will hit pretax profits by 20 million for the year as a whole.
